answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates immediate churn pressure on price-sensitive SMB, but memory_73 provides clear evidence that promotional pricing at that segment does not retain cohorts through renewal—it merely shifts acquisition timing and damages LTV. Rather than match a losing strategy, redirect resources to defensible, high-margin channels. memory_44 demonstrates enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows with superior pipeline quality. memory_57 shows referral incentives among established customers generate qualified revenue without retention harm. memory_91 confirms activation messaging drives early engagement. A two-part standard experiment: (1) activate sales-assist resources to develop enterprise pipeline with superior unit economics and longer contract terms—these accounts are insulated from price-competition and align with primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue; (2) deploy targeted referral incentives to established customers to convert them into growth multipliers, leveraging their lower churn risk. This avoids the discount trap while building defensible revenue channels. The SMB price-sensitive cohort is not worth retaining through margin-destructive discounting given their demonstrated renewal failure pattern.
